fields.name: Nominal amount
fields.definition: Quantity * nominal unit amount
fields.comment:
EIOPA definition (06.02 and 08.01). Applicable to instruments with CIC-codes 1,2,5,6,72,73,74, 8 and derivatives. Principle amount outstanding measured at par amount, for all assets where this item is relevant, and at nominal amount for CIC = 72, 73, 74, 75 and 79 if applicable.

For futures and options corresponds to contract size multiplied by the trigger value and by the number of contracts reported in that line. For swaps and forwards it corresponds to the contract amount of the contracts reported in that line. When the trigger value corresponds to a range, the average value of the range shall be used.
The notional amount refers to the amount that is being hedged / invested (when not covering risks). If several trades occur, it shall be the net amount at the reporting date. Buy gives +; sale gives -

fields.name: Market exposure amount in quotation currency (A)
fields.definition: Market exposure amount different from market valuation for derivatives (valuation of the equivalent position on the underlying asset)
fields.comment:
For equity future contracts, index futures contracts and options etc. data is calculated depending on characteristics of the contract (quantity, contract size, strike price etc.) and the index value or underlying value. 
Example: ESTX 50 Index Future: quantity (79) x contract size (10) x index market value (3.145) = 2.484.550 EUR Exposure. 
For options: quantity (79) x contract size (10) * Last valuation price of the underlying (72) *  Sensitivity to underlying asset price (delta) (93). 
For the fixed income future contracts this data is equal to the exposure resulting on the cheapest to deliver (analogous to the preceding calculations for equity contracts). 
For FRA contracts, FX-Forwards and CDS this data is the notional amount 
This amount is signed

fields.name: Market exposure amount in portfolio currency (B)
fields.definition: Market exposure amount different from market valuation for derivatives (valuation of the equivalent position on the underlying asset) in the quotation currency of the portfolio
fields.comment:
This field used for FX exposures, equity exposures, credit and interest rates; using the following rules:
* exposure on derivatives are deriving from equivalent exposure on simple underlying instruments without considering type of risk to be evaluated
*both Put and CDS should have negative exposures and positive quantities or nominal amounts for long positions, with positive exposure for short positions 
*residual maturity should be handled by information system that will do SCR calculations and produce QRTs
* exposure on cash or equivalent should be egal to the valuation ( exposure for interest rate risks should be obtained by multiplying the amount by the modified duration (field 90) and for credit risk by credit sensitivity (field 91)
 * exposure for options or convertible bond instruments should be used by multiplying the exposure by the delta for the relevant risk category.
This amount is signed

fields.name: Interest rate type
fields.definition:
* Fixed - plain vanilla fixed coupon rate
* Floating - plain vanilla floating coupon rates (for all interest rates, which refer to a reference interest rate like EONIA or EURIBOR + margin in BP)
* Variable - all other variable interest rates like step-up or step-down or fixed-to-float bonds. The variable feature is the (credit) margin or the change between fixed and float.
* Inflation_linked for inflation linked bonds in order to identify them.
fields.comment:
For step up bonds only ongoing period characteristics are entered. 
Floating example : a bond with a coupon rate of EONIA or EURIBOR + xxx bp
Variable example : a fixed to float bond with a fixed coupon until 31/12/2040 then a floating coupon of EURIBOR + xxxbp. This bond will be modelled as Variable until 31/12/2040 then Floating until redemption
Inflation linked example : a bond with a nominal and a coupon rate embedding an inflation index component

fields.name: Coupon rate
fields.definition:
Fixed rate: coupon rate as a percentage of nominal amount
Floating rate: last fixing rate + margin as a percentage of nominal amount
Variable rate: estimation of current rate over the period + margin as a percentage of nominal amount
all rates are expressed on an annual basis
fields.comment:
This field should be filled with the current coupon rate expressed as a percentage of the nominal amount.  It is expressed in a different way from weights (fields 26 and 30 for example).  
Example: bond with  fixed 1.5 % coupon to show as "1.5".  A  floater euribor3m + 0.20% to show as "0.26" provided the last fixing was 0.06% for the euribor3m.

fields.name: Securitisation
fields.definition: Securitisation typology
fields.codification:
alpha (1)
"a" refers to the fact that the asset managers have not assessed the eligibility of a treatment of the securitisation positions under Solvency II
"b" refers to security positions eligible for art 178 (3) and art 178 (5) (Senior STS)
"c" refers to security positions eligible for art 178 (4) and art 178 (6)  (Junior STS)
"d" refers to resecuritisation positions as per art 178(7)  (re-securitisation)
"e1" refers to securitisation positions as per Art 178 (8) . (senior non STS)
"e2" refers to securitisation positions as per Art 178 (8a). (junior non STS)
"e3" refers to securitisation positions as per Art 178 (9 ).  (others)
"f" refers to security positions eligible for art 178a (1) & (2) (transitional regime for type 1 securitisations without new underlying exposure since the 01/01/2019)
"g" refers to security positions eligible for art 178a (3)  (transitional regime for some type 1 securitisations on residential mortgages)
"h"refers to security positions eligible for art 178a (4)  (transitional regime for some type 1 securitisations on residential mortgages)
"i" refers to security positions eligible for art 180 (10) and art 180 (10a). (Securitisation secured by the EIB or the EIF) 
"j" refers to security positions that have been analysed and shall not be considered as "securitisation " under Solvency 2 (No securitisation).
fields.comment:
Used for synthetic ABS (synthetic asset backed securities, CDO etc.) and other ABS Or Structured Products only.
Participant shall not fill this fields for assets other than CIC 5 or CIC 6. 
Particpant shall fill "a" or "j" for structured notes or collateralized securities that are not considered as securisations.

fields.name: Bond floor (convertible instrument only)
fields.section: Specific data for convertible bonds - optional (pricing of convertible bonds using shock modelling)
fields.definition: Lowest value of a convertible bond expressed in quotation currency, at current issuer spread
fields.comment: The lowest value that convertible bonds can fall to, given the present value of the remaining future cash flows and principal repayment. The bond floor is the value at which the convertible option becomes worthless because the underlying stock price has fallen substantially below the conversion value

fields.name: Option premium (convertible instrument only)
fields.section: Specific data for convertible bonds - optional (pricing of convertible bonds using shock modelling)
fields.definition: Premium of the embedded option of a convertible bond in quotation currency
fields.comment: The amount by which the price of a convertible security exceeds the current market value of the common stock into which it may be converted. A conversion premium is the difference between the price of the convertible and the greater of the conversion or straight-bond value.

fields.name: LTEI Fund Eligibility
fields.definition: Eligibility of the held fund to LTEI dispositions according to regulation
fields.comment:
According to the article 171d of RD UE 2015/35 revised some collective investment undertakings with a lower risk profile can be eligible to Long term equity Investments dispositions and benefit from a reduced capital charge. 
This datapoint allow insurance company to identify funds held in the portfolio that can benefit from these dispositions provided the asset manager provide this analysis as an additional service.
 The rational for this added datapoint relies in allowing consistency with SCR calculation eventually provided in the TPT and indicating wether equity held in dedicated private equity funds are eligible.

fields.name: Legislative program investment
fields.definition: Eligibility of the held equities to legislative programmes dispositions
fields.comment:
According to the article 173 of RD UE 2015/35 investments in equity, either directly or through collective investment undertakings under some legislative programs may benefit from a reduction in capital charge
This datapoint allow insurance company to identify instruments held in the portfolio that can benefit from these dispositions provided the asset manager provide this analysis as an additional service.
